Here’s a quick roundup of some of the most highly regarded crime‑thriller films released in 2020. These picks span a range of styles—from gritty noir to high‑stakes heists—and have been praised by critics and audiences alike.

| # | Title | Director | Key Cast | Why It Stands Out |
|---|-------|----------|----------|-------------------|
| 1 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | A modern take on the classic horror trope, this film blends psychological suspense with a strong feminist angle. Its tight pacing and Moss’s compelling performance keep viewers on edge. |
| 2 | **The Gentlemen** | Guy Ritchie | Matthew McConaughey, Charlie Hunnam, Michelle Dockery | Ritchie's signature fast‑cut style and witty dialogue make this gangster caper both entertaining and cleverly plotted. |
| 3 | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | Ewan McGregor, Sacha Baron Cohen, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II | Though more courtroom drama than traditional thriller, its tense legal battles and historical context give it a gripping edge. |
| 4 | **The Hunt** | Thomas Vinterberg | Mads Mikkelsen, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau | A chilling exploration of paranoia and mob mentality, this film’s raw performances and bleak atmosphere create a tense narrative. |
| 5 | **The Nightingale** | Jennifer Kent | Lily James, David Wenham | Set in 19th‑century Australia, this revenge thriller combines historical detail with visceral action sequences. |
| 6 | **The Last Duel** | Ridley Scott | Matt Damon, Adam Driver, Jodie Comer | A medieval duel turned crime‑thriller, this film offers a unique blend of historical drama and suspenseful storytelling. |
| 7 | **The Devil All the Time** | Antonio Campos | Tom Holland, Robert Pattinson, Riley Keough | A dark, atmospheric tale of crime and corruption in rural America, it’s praised for its haunting visuals and strong ensemble cast. |
| 8 | **The Little Things** | John Lee Hancock | Denzel Washington, Rami Malek, Jared Leto | A modern detective mystery that balances character study with procedural intrigue, featuring standout performances from Washington and Malek. |
| 9 | **The Woman in the Window** | Andrew Dominik | Amy Adams, Daniel Brühl | A psychological thriller about an agoraphobic woman who witnesses a crime, it’s noted for its tense atmosphere and twisty plot. |
|10 | **The Invisible Man** (TV series) | Leigh Whannell | Elisabeth Moss, Oliver Jackson-Cohen | While technically a TV series, its first season was released in 2020 and offers a fresh, suspenseful take on the classic story. |

### How to Watch

- **Streaming Platforms:** Many of these titles are available on Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, Hulu, or HBO Max. Check your local listings or use a streaming aggregator like JustWatch to find where each film is currently hosted.
- **Physical Media:** If you prefer Blu‑ray or DVD, most of these films have been released on physical media and can be purchased online or at local retailers.

Enjoy diving into these crime‑thrillers! If you’d like more details on any particular film—such as release dates, ratings, or behind‑the‑scenes trivia—just let me know.
